text: dsh-tool-docx 是面向 DSH 的 Microsoft Word 文档工具插件，通过工具服务注册 docx_read、docx_create 和 docx_edit。读取工具可将 .docx 内容提取为 Markdown 或结构化 JSON 块，并返回文档属性；创建工具把包含标题、段落、列表、表格和行内格式的 Markdown 写成新的 Word 文件；编辑工具以 Markdown 替换文档正文并保留标题、作者和创建时间属性。插件还提供二进制文件写入服务供不原生支持二进制写入的主机使用。适合需要让 DSH 助手读写办公文档的场景；代码未声明 API Key 或外部账号要求。

dsh-tool-docx adds Word tools to DSH. docx_read extracts .docx files as Markdown or JSON; docx_create makes Word files from Markdown; docx_edit replaces document content while retaining title, author, and creation properties. A binary filesystem writer is also included.
想让 DSH 把 Word 文档转成 Markdown 方便阅读。
能不能把 docx 的内容提取成结构化 JSON？
帮我根据 Markdown 生成一个新的 Word 文件。
我想用 Markdown 修改已有 DOCX 文档并保留文档属性。
Can DSH read a Word document and return Markdown or structured blocks?
Create a .docx file from Markdown using my DSH assistant.
dsh-tool-docx 的功能「读取 Word 文档」：调用 docx_read 并提供 .docx 路径，可选择输出 Markdown（默认）或结构化 JSON 块；结果还包含标题、作者、创建时间等属性。
dsh-tool-docx 的功能「从 Markdown 创建或编辑 Word」：docx_create 将 Markdown 转为新 .docx；docx_edit 用完整的新 Markdown 替换正文，同时保留标题、作者和创建时间。

dsh-tool-docx README · dsh-tool-docx：Model-facing Microsoft Word (`.docx`) tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): `docx_read` extracts a document as Markdown or structured JSON blocks, `docx_create` generates a new `.docx` from Markdown, and `docx_edit` replaces a document's content from Markdown while preserving its title/author/created properties. `.docx` is a ZIP of XML parts, so every tool reads the whole package through the bounded `ctx.fs.readBytes` primitive and writes packages through the plugin's `fsBinary` binary write service (or a host `ctx.fs` that provides `writeBytes` natively) — the same atomic, sandbox-fenced mutations the text tools use, without ever replacing the host's own filesystem.

dsh-tool-docx README · dsh-tool-docx：This repository is the **standalone distribution** of the plugin. The plugin is **original work written for DeepSeek Harness** — an independent plugin developed by this project, initially in a local `deepseek-harness` checkout (the harness is its runtime target), not a copy of a plugin from the shared repository. It plugs into the harness's `tools`, `fs`, and `systemPrompt` services, and it builds and tests on its own against the published `@deepseek-ai/*` packages, so it can be installed into any harness checkout.

dsh-tool-docx README · Requirements：- A DeepSeek Harness host (the `0.1.0-rc.7` line) whose filesystem seam provides the **read** primitive `fs.readBytes` — published in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs` since `0.1.0-rc.7`. The **write** side (`writeBytes`) is not in any published `dsh-fs` release, so the bundle mounts the plugin's [binary fs providers](#binary-fs-providers): a separate `fsBinary` service that implements `writeBytes` (fenced for sandboxed hosts) without touching `ctx.fs`. Without any binary writer — no `fsBinary` service and no native `ctx.fs.writeBytes` — `docx_read` still works, while `docx_create`/`docx_edit` fail with a typed `DOCX_HOST_FS_UNSUPPORTED` error naming the fix.
- The harness provides the peer services (the `0.1.0-rc.7` line): `cordis`, `dsh-tools`, `dsh-fs`, `dsh-llm`, `dsh-sandbox`, `dsh-sandbox-policy`, `dsh-system-prompt`, `dsh-invariants`, `dsh-user-approval`, `dsh-session`.

dsh-tool-docx README · Installation：The official install path is the harness's own plugin manager — one command installs the package into the profile, and the profile launcher activates the bundle's [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) layer automatically (the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tool-docx
```

dsh-tool-docx README · Installation：`dsh plugin` runs pnpm inside the profile directory and reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles` against the installed state, so nothing else is needed — no `allowBuilds` entries (the package ships its built `lib/` and has no build scripts), no manual `cordis.patch.yml` editing, no `--patch` overlays. Restart the harness afterwards.

dsh-tool-docx README · Installation：- **Update:** `dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-tool-docx`, or re-run `add` with the new tag.
- **Remove:** `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-tool-docx`.
- **Local development:** `dsh plugin --profile web add ../dsh-tool-docx` (relative specs are anchored to the directory you invoke from) or `dsh plugin --profile web add link:../dsh-tool-docx`.

dsh-tool-docx README · Installation：> Published on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tool-docx) as `dsh-tool-docx` (the `dsh-tool-*` ecosystem convention), independent of the `@deepseek-ai` scope.

dsh-tool-docx README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docx_read(file_path, format?, max_chars?)` | Extract document body as Markdown (default) or structured JSON blocks plus `docProps`. When the `attachments` service is mounted, embedded images are extracted from `word/media/*` and returned as durable image content blocks alongside the text. Emits `fs/observed`. |
| `docx_create(file_path, markdown, title?, author?)` | Generate a new `.docx` from Markdown. Embeds images referenced in the markdown (``) by reading them from the filesystem. Guarded `createIfAbsent`: an existing file is never blindly overwritten. |
| `docx_edit(file_path, markdown)` | Read the current document (validating it is a docx), preserve `docProps` and embedded images, regenerate the body from the full Markdown, and write back with a version guard (`DOCX_STALE` on a concurrent change). New image references in the markdown are resolved from the filesystem. |

dsh-tool-docx README · Tools：All three resolve relative paths against the calling agent's session cwd, dispatch the `fs/write-intent` waterfall before mutating (the observation-policy plugin may supply its own intent), and record `fs/observed` on completion — so the sandbox fence, escalation fields, and read-before-write policy apply to docx mutations exactly as they do to `write`/`edit`.

dsh-tool-docx README · Config：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxDocxBytes` | 64 MiB | Inclusive byte cap on a whole `.docx` file (read + ZIP expansion). |
| `maxMarkdownChars` | 1 000 000 | Inclusive character cap on the Markdown input to create/edit. |
| `maxReadChars` | 200 000 | Inclusive character cap on the Markdown returned by `docx_read`. |

dsh-tool-docx README · Binary fs providers：The base bundle's `fs-sandbox` row keeps providing `ctx.fs` **unchanged**. The bundle patch adds the docx tools plus one of the binary providers, which register the binary `writeBytes` primitive as a **separate `fsBinary` service** — the host filesystem is never replaced, so this plugin cannot break the harness boot; at worst, without the provider, the mutating tools report `DOCX_HOST_FS_UNSUPPORTED`:

dsh-tool-docx README · Binary fs providers：- **`dsh-tool-docx/fs-binary-sandbox-plugin`** (mounted by the bundle; recommended for sandboxed hosts) — registers `fsBinary.writeBytes` fenced by the **same per-call policy** as every sandbox mutation: `workspace-write` containment, `read-only` denial, `danger-full-access` passthrough, `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` on refusal (mapped to `DOCX_SANDBOX_DENIED` at the tool layer).
- **`dsh-tool-docx/fs-binary-local-plugin`** — registers `fsBinary.writeBytes` **unfenced**, for minimal contexts (tests, headless scripts) or hosts that fence above the provider. To mount it instead of the sandboxed one, override the bundle row in your profile `cordis.patch.yml`:

dsh-tool-docx README · Binary fs providers：```yaml
  - id: fs-binary-sandbox
    disabled: true
  - insert:
      - id: fs-binary-local

dsh-tool-docx README · Binary fs providers：Both use the same probe → intent-guard (`createIfAbsent` / `replaceIfVersion`) → atomic-publish flow as the harness seam: a private owner-only staging directory, fsync, then atomic publication (a hard-link no-replace primitive for `createIfAbsent`), with per-target serialization. The first version omits the harness's Win32 DACL-preservation ceremony — a replacement inherits the owner-only ACL of the staged temp file.

dsh-tool-docx README · Binary fs providers：For hosts that deliberately want the full backend mounted **as `ctx.fs`** (replacing `fs-sandbox`), the package also ships the provider classes `dsh-tool-docx/fs-binary-sandbox` and `dsh-tool-docx/fs-binary-local`; the replace-the-row recipe still applies:

```yaml
- id: fs-sandbox
  disabled: true
- insert:
    - id: fs-binary-sandbox

dsh-tool-docx README · Design notes：- **Extraction** (`src/docx/extract.ts`) walks `word/document.xml` with `fast-xml-parser`: headings (`Heading1`–`Heading6`, `Title`), bold/italic/strike runs, nested lists through `word/numbering.xml` (bullet vs decimal), pipe tables (merged cells approximate), external hyperlinks through `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`, and embedded images as counted placeholders. Unsupported constructs degrade to warnings, never failures.
- **Generation** (`src/docx/generate.ts`) renders the block model with the `docx` library: ATX headings, styled inline runs, 9-level bullet/numbered numbering, pipe tables, and `[text](url)` external hyperlinks. `parseMarkdown` (src/markdown.ts) accepts the subset the extractor emits, so read → edit → write round trips are stable.
- **Caps are enforced at the seam, not in the tool** — the whole-file byte cap flows into `ctx.fs.readBytes` (`FS_TOO_LARGE` maps to `DOCX_TOO_LARGE`), and the ZIP reader applies the same cap to the uncompressed total, so a compressed bomb cannot expand without limit.
- **Sandbox parity** — `src/sandbox.ts` mirrors `dsh-tool-fs`'s escalation API (`sandbox_permissions`/`justification` advertised only u
dsh-tool-docx README · What the model sees：The `tool:docx-read` section below is registered once at plugin apply:

dsh-tool-docx README · The docx guidance section：```markdown
MS Word .docx files are binary (ZIP+XML) and the read tool cannot read them. Use docx_read to extract a document as Markdown (default) or structured JSON blocks, docx_create to generate a new .docx from Markdown, and docx_edit to replace a document's content from Markdown while preserving its title/author/created properties. Legacy .doc is not supported — convert it to .docx first.
```
dsh-tool-docx README · Token effect：Fixed guidance cost per request while the plugin is mounted; the section is unaffected by scoped tool restrictions.
dsh-tool-docx README · KV Cache effect：Prefix-stable while the guidance text is unchanged. Plugin lifecycle or a text change may invalidate reuse from the first changed prompt section.

dsh-tool-docx README · What the model sees：The generated `docx_read`, `docx_create`, and `docx_edit` schemas — parameters and canonical outputs as summarized in the [Tools](#tools) table. The byte/character caps are deployment settings, not model arguments; the escalation fields appear only under a confining filesystem backend.
dsh-tool-docx README · Token effect：Fixed schema cost per request for each mounted tool; config disablement removes schemas and guidance together, while a scoped restriction removes only the schema.

dsh-tool-docx README · KV Cache effect：Prefix-stable while definitions and visibility are unchanged. Config enablement, plugin lifecycle, or scoped restrictions may invalidate reuse from the first changed schema token.

dsh-tool-docx README · What the model sees：A successful `docx_read` renders the extracted Markdown (or pretty-printed JSON blocks). When the `attachments` service is mounted and the document contains images, the tool result also carries `{ type: 'image', attachment }` content blocks — the model sees the images directly, without a separate `read_image` call. Truncation appends `\n… (truncated)`; failures are typed messages such as `file not found: <path>`, `the document is encrypted (password-protected); decryption is not supported`, or the legacy hint `legacy .doc format is not supported — convert the document to .docx first`.
dsh-tool-docx README · Token effect：Data-dependent results are capped by `maxReadChars` (or the call's `max_chars`) and resent until compaction.
dsh-tool-docx README · KV Cache effect：Append-only; newly visible content follows the reusable request prefix and does not invalidate existing KV-cache entries.

dsh-tool-docx README · What the model sees：A successful create/edit renders a short `<path>`/`<type>docx</type>` envelope with the byte size — never the document body. Warnings about approximations (images, merged cells, code blocks) are carried in the canonical `warnings` array and rendered as plain text.
dsh-tool-docx README · Token effect：Only the retained call arguments (including the full Markdown input) and the short result add tokens; the generated package bytes never enter the session log.
dsh-tool-docx README · KV Cache effect：Append-only; newly visible content follows the reusable request prefix and does not invalidate existing KV-cache entries.

dsh-tool-docx README · What the model sees：Blank `file_path` becomes `Error: file_path must be a non-empty string`; markdown over the input cap becomes `Error: markdown exceeds the <n>-character limit`.
dsh-tool-docx README · Token effect：Only the failing call adds these retained tokens.
dsh-tool-docx README · KV Cache effect：Append-only; newly visible content follows the reusable request prefix and does not invalidate existing KV-cache entries.

dsh-tool-docx README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Legacy `.doc` (OLE) is unsupported** — binary OLE needs LibreOffice or Word COM conversion; the tools fail with `DOCX_LEGACY_DOC` and a hint to convert to `.docx` first.
- **Round-trip regenerates the document** — styles, page setup, headers/footers, and section breaks are not preserved; an edit rebuilds the body with default styles, keeping only title/author/created and embedded images. Layout fidelity is not a goal of the round trip.
- **Merged table cells approximate** — `gridSpan`/`vMerge` degrade to plain pipe-table cells with a warning; footnotes, endnotes, text boxes, and page breaks are dropped (warnings included).
- **The sandbox controller duplicates `dsh-tool-fs`** — extracting a shared `FsSandboxController` is deferred; the two copies must be kept in sync until then.
- **Markdown input subset** — blockquotes, horizontal rules, and nested fences are not represented; they degrade to paragraphs with a warning (fenced code becomes code-styled paragraphs).
- **Structured error codes under the tsx source run** — when the harness launches from source (`node --import tsx/esm`, the dev launcher), the healed `$DSH_HOM

dsh-tool-docx README · Relationship to deepseek-harness：This plugin is an **original, independent project written for DeepSeek Harness** — it plugs into the harness's public services (`tools`, `fs`, `systemPrompt`) and is developed in a local `deepseek-harness` checkout for testing against the harness. It is not a copy of a plugin from the shared `deepseek-harness` repository and is not part of it; this repository is the canonical distribution. Two implementation notes:

dsh-tool-docx README · Relationship to deepseek-harness：1. `src/fs-binary.ts` (host contract + writer resolver) — the binary `readBytes`/`writeBytes` contract is part of this plugin's design. `readBytes` is published in the harness's `dsh-fs` release line since `0.1.0-rc.7`; `writeBytes` is not, so the [binary fs providers](#binary-fs-providers) ship it as a separate `fsBinary` service instead of patching the host;
2. `tests/` runs against the published `ToolRuntime` service (exported since `dsh-tools@0.1.0-rc.7`), so the consumer tests exercise the real registry pipeline rather than a local double.

dsh-tool-docx README · Relationship to deepseek-harness：The plugin is developed and maintained entirely in this repository against the published `@deepseek-ai/*` packages; the harness checkout is only a runtime target used for integration verification, and carries no copy of this plugin.
